input:
Earlier scenes:
很久以前，古代的人很不知道什么植物能吃，也什么植物不能吃。所以很多人常常吃不安全的植物，吃不安全的植物对你的身体有坏处，很麻烦的情况。但是一个人，神农，要解决这个问题。他又聪明又努力，旅行很远找到很多植物。比方说，灵芝和夹竹桃。他一吃各种各样的植物就知道能不能吃这些植物。然后，神农写他的主意。他喜欢植物的味道，特别是花。神农遇到了一个黄色的花，一吃就觉得不舒服。

This scene:
发现了夹竹桃有毒。别人看到他，很快给他吃一个灵芝。神农一吃就觉得比较好。然后，他继续写他发现的信息。会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能不能吃。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 发现了夹竹桃有毒：it is unclear that夹竹桃refers to黄色的花
- 别人看到他：另外一个人，“别(的)” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”, whereas “另外“ is for “addition in quantity”, and “another, the other”
- 会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能不能吃：也会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能吃，哪个植物不能吃

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 别人：一个男人，别人 distinguishes other people from an already established speaker or group; no such group has been established here, so introduce the new helper with a noun phrase. [teacher rule: bieren]
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 给他吃一个灵芝：给了他一个灵芝吃，this is a completed rescue action, so the verb 给 needs 了. [rule: aspect_le_completed]
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 写他发现的信息：写下他发现的信息，写 means to write or compose, while 写下 means to record information so it is kept. [vocab list]
4. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 哪一个植物能不能吃：哪一种植物能吃，哪一种植物不能吃，哪一个 asks which single item, while 能不能 asks a yes-or-no question; use parallel clauses to explain which plants are edible and which are not. [rule: none]

items.reason: 别人 cannot introduce this single new helper here; 一个男人 is a grammatical new-person noun phrase.
给他吃一个灵芝 is acceptable in this narrative, so 了 is not required.
写他发现的信息 is already a natural way to say that he writes the information he discovered.
哪一个植物能不能吃 improperly combines a which-item question with a yes-or-no question, and the parallel correction resolves it.
